main_body: Japanese townhouse seen straight on: a large blue-grey tile roof with a ridge, a cream plaster band, a lower eave roof, and a brown lattice storefront with a dark doorway
top_band: x=47: rows 1-5 form a thin blue-grey ridge band (L 83-158). Rows 6-28 are the roof tiles in one dark tone (L 56). Rows 33-40 are cream plaster (L 221), not a top surface.
evidence: The whole piece is stacked vertical bands: ridge, roof, plaster wall, lower roof, lattice front. The roof tiles are drawn as vertical stripes facing the viewer, like a panel. There are no hip or side slopes and no foreshortened horizontal top surface. The only top-like band is the 5-row ridge strip, and it is not separated from the roof by a front-edge line. The lower eave (rows 41-47) is a flat strip with no shadow row beneath it. The lattice and door are painted flat on the face. It reads as a front elevation with decoration, not a 3/4 building like the references with their visible roof planes.

style.evidence: The measured facts are well below the references. The candidate has 8 colours per tile against 11 and 18, and 34 distinct colours against 66 and 185. 72% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% for the references, so the outline is mostly neutral dark rather than tinted to the material. The roof has about 5 blue-grey steps with some per-tile variation, and flat-fill coverage is only 3%. The overall look is thinner and more sticker-like than the references, whose roofs have scalloped tiles with highlights and whose walls have grain. The wall and lattice areas are simple.
